usage: The phrase 'daa2 gung1' means to work for someone, typically referring to employment under an employer.
It is commonly used to describe part-time or full-time jobs, especially in informal contexts.
This expression can apply to various types of work, ranging from manual labor to office jobs.
In conversation, 'daa2 gung1' can describe both temporary and long-term employment situations.
It is often used to contrast with self-employment or running one's own business.

examples.sentence: 我而家喺餐廳打工，忙到冇時間休息。
examples.jyutping: ngo5 ji4 gaa1 hai2 caan1 teng1 daa2 gung1, mong4 dou3 mou5 si4 gaan3 jau1 sik1.
examples.meaning: I am currently working in a restaurant, so busy that I have no time to rest.

examples.sentence: 細佬啱啱開始喺間旅行社打工。
examples.jyutping: sai3 lou2 ngaam1 ngaam1 hoi1 ci2 hai2 gaan1 leoi5 hang4 se5 daa2 gung1.
examples.meaning: My younger brother just started working at a travel agency.

examples.sentence: 好多學生暑假嚟呢度打工賺零用錢。
examples.jyutping: hou2 do1 hok6 saang1 syu1 gaa3 lei4 ni1 dou6 daa2 gung1 zaan6 ling4 jung6 cin2.
examples.meaning: Many students come here during summer vacation to work and earn pocket money.

examples.sentence: 我唔想一世都喺度打工，想自己做老闆。
examples.jyutping: ngo5 m4 soeng2 jat1 sai3 dou1 hai2 dou6 daa2 gung1, soeng2 zi6 gei2 zou6 lou5 baan2.
examples.meaning: I don't want to work for others all my life; I want to be my own boss.
